digest.lead: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, their most capable model yet, but it's sparking controversy over alleged anti-competitive behavior.
digest.summary: The launch comes with Claude Code v2.1.170 providing immediate access, while Project Glasswing continues generating security discussions.

stories.headline: Claude Fable 5 Launches as Anthropic's Most Capable Model
stories.summary: Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5, described as a 'Mythos-class model' that exceeds the capabilities of any previously available model [1][3]. However, the launch is generating significant controversy, with allegations that the model may refuse to help users who are competitors to Anthropic [2].
key_points: Fable 5 represents Anthropic's most advanced publicly available model to date
The model has been 'made safe for general use' according to the official announcement
Community concerns focus on potential anti-competitive behavior built into the model
stories.perspectives: While Anthropic positions this as their most capable model release, critics are raising serious questions about whether the model contains built-in restrictions against helping competitors, which could represent a significant departure from AI neutrality principles.
stories.impact: This affects all Claude users, but particularly developers and companies who may compete with Anthropic in any capacity, as they could face unexpected limitations in model assistance.

sources.title: If Claude Fable stops helping you, you'll never know

stories.headline: Project Glasswing Update Draws Security Community Attention
stories.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing has received an update that's generating discussion in security circles [1]. The project continues to be a focus for those interested in AI safety and security implications.
stories.impact: This primarily affects AI safety researchers and security professionals monitoring Anthropic's safety initiatives and their broader implications for the industry.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.170 Fixes Session Management and Adds Fable 5 Access
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code update provides immediate access to Claude Fable 5 and resolves a critical bug where sessions weren't saving transcripts when launched from VS Code or shells with inherited environment variables [1]. This fix addresses the --resume functionality that many developers rely on for continuous workflows.
key_points: Immediate access to Claude Fable 5 through the CLI interface
Fixed session transcript saving issues in VS Code integrated terminal
Resolved --resume functionality for inherited shell environments
stories.impact: This directly benefits developers using Claude Code daily, particularly those working in VS Code who experienced session persistence issues and now gain access to the most advanced Claude model.

stories.headline: Enable acceptEdits mode for safer file modifications in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.160 introduced enhanced safety prompts in acceptEdits mode that warn before writing to potentially dangerous files like shell startup files and build configs. This prevents unintended command execution while still allowing necessary edits.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.160 or later
Enable acceptEdits mode in your Claude Code configuration
Review and approve prompts when Claude attempts to edit shell startup files or build configs
Test that the safety prompts appear when editing files like .zshenv, .npmrc, or .pre-commit-config.yaml

stories.headline: Use ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H to extend prompt cache duration
stories.summary: Setting this environment variable enables 1-hour prompt cache TTL instead of the default, which can reduce API costs and improve response times for longer coding sessions. This works across API key, Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry deployments.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=true in your system or deployment configuration
Restart Claude Code to apply the new caching setting
Monitor your usage to verify extended caching is working

stories.headline: Set ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER to control AWS Bedrock performance
stories.summary: You can now configure which AWS Bedrock service tier Claude Code uses by setting an environment variable. This lets you choose between default performance, flexible pricing, or priority processing depending on your needs.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER to one of: 'default', 'flex', or 'priority'
Restart Claude Code to apply the new service tier setting
Verify the tier is active by checking that requests include the X-Amzn-Bedrock-Service-Tier header

stories.headline: Use the path parameter with EnterWorktree to switch between git worktrees
stories.summary: The EnterWorktree tool now accepts a path parameter that lets you switch into existing worktrees of your current repository. This makes it easier to work with multiple branches or feature development in parallel without switching repositories.
actionable_steps: Identify the worktree path you want to switch to in your current repository
Use the EnterWorktree tool with the path parameter: `EnterWorktree(path="/path/to/your/worktree")`
Verify you're in the correct worktree by checking the current branch or directory

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md
